facts.text: The stop criterion for creating virtual job sites should use requirement coverage, parameter-space coverage, reality coverage and residual model uncertainty rather than a site count.
facts.quote: Rather than a site count, four questions:

facts.text: Requirement coverage for virtual job-site testing asks whether all identified risk areas, object classes and machine motions have been tested.
facts.quote: requirement coverage (have all identified risk areas, object classes and machine motions been tested?)

facts.text: Parameter-space coverage for virtual job-site testing asks whether the selected interactions and boundaries have been covered.
facts.quote: parameter-space coverage (have the selected interactions and boundaries been covered?)

facts.text: Reality coverage for virtual job-site testing asks whether the virtual distribution reproduces the geometric, sensor and ground characteristics measured in the field.
facts.quote: reality coverage (does the virtual distribution reproduce the geometric, sensor and ground characteristics measured in the field?)

facts.text: Residual model uncertainty as a stop criterion for virtual job-site testing asks whether simulator-to-physical discrepancies stay below the acceptance limits for each test assertion.
facts.quote: residual model uncertainty (do simulator-to-physical discrepancies stay below the acceptance limits for each test assertion?)

facts.text: A simulator that predicts detection well but braking distance poorly can be valid for perception regression and invalid for a final collision or no-collision assertion.
facts.quote: a simulator that predicts detection well but braking distance poorly can be valid for perception regression and invalid for a final collision or no-collision assertion.
